name: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (Royal Saudi Land Forces and Saudi Arabian National Guard)
callout_language: Gulf Arabic military radio: 'ishtibak' (contact), 'nar' (fire), 'qunbula' (grenade), 'musab' (wounded), 'tayyara bidun tayyar' / 'dron' (drone); English loanwords from US/UK training.

doctrine.summary: A well-funded Western-equipped force split between the Royal Saudi Land Forces (armoured and mechanised brigades on Abrams, Bradley, M113) and the Saudi Arabian National Guard (a separate tribal-loyal force on LAV wheeled vehicles and CAESAR guns), plus Border Guards and special forces. Combat experience comes from the war in Yemen (2015-2022 intervention, truce since 2022), where air power, local Yemeni allies and border defence carried most of the load. Doctrine leans on air superiority, Patriot/THAAD air defence and fortified border posts. Since February 2026 Saudi Arabia has been struck by Iran, the Houthis and Iraqi militias; it struck back at Iran, signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement with Türkiye and Pakistan (August 2026) and in October 2026 agreed to host Turkish and Pakistani deployments under it.
doctrine.fireteam: US-style infantry squad of 9 in two fireteams around a Minimi/MG3, riding in a Bradley, M113 or LAV. Special forces and border guard teams of 6-8. In game: 8 men in battle-buddy pairs.
tactics: Heavy reliance on air strikes and attack helicopters before ground movement
Fortified border posts and observation towers along the Yemen frontier (yemen_red_sea)
Mechanised convoys with MRAP and Humvee escorts; route clearance against IEDs
Local allied Yemeni forces lead infantry assaults while Saudi units provide fire support
Layered air and drone defence (Patriot, THAAD, Skyguard, counter-UAS) around oil and urban sites
Special forces raids against AQAP and smuggling networks

camo.name: Multicam-type (special forces)
camo.use: Special Security Forces and Army special forces

launchers: RPG-7 captured or for allied Yemeni forces [in_game]

body_armor.notes: Modern aramid helmets and plate carriers with ceramic front/back plates in front-line and special units = medium. Border posts and reservists often lighter.

vehicles.notes: M1A2S Abrams (several lost to Houthi ATGMs on the border, 2015-17); M1A2S SEP v3 upgrade ordered.
M2A2 Bradley IFVs of the Royal Saudi Land Forces.
SANG wheeled fleet: LAV-25/LAV II and the large 2014 LAV 6 order (assault, ATGM, mortar, command variants).
M60A3 still in service in reserve/second-line brigades.
M113A2/A3 family and M577 command vehicles.
Up-armoured Humvees with M2/TOW for patrol and border units.
M-ATVs and other MRAPs bought for the Yemen border.
Border Guard and special-forces Land Cruiser pickups with MGs.
SANG CAESAR 155 mm truck-mounted guns; M109A5 with the army.
Chinese Wing Loong II armed drones; also domestic Saqr and Turkish drones on order.

unlocks: Steyr AUG and HK G36 rifles
plate carriers with ceramic front/back plates
Toyota Land Cruiser and Humvee purchase (unarmed)

notes: Early-game client: the Yemen frontier and Red Sea coast give counter-AQAP, anti-smuggling and border-defence contracts, and since 2026 counter-drone work against Houthi, Iraqi-militia and Iranian strikes. Political context 2026: Saudi-Houthi truce since 2022 broken by renewed strikes after the Iran war began (28 February 2026) and the Houthi Bab al-Mandab escalation (September 2026); Saudi Arabia struck Iran after being attacked; Mecca Joint Defence Agreement with Türkiye and Pakistan (7 August 2026), collective-defence deployments agreed 5 October 2026; Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement with Pakistan from September 2025. Relations with the UAE cooled after the December 2025 Yemen crisis over the Southern Transitional Council. No diplomatic relations with Israel. Backs Syria's new government. Real-world operator records only; any game assignment of Abrams/Bradley/M-ATV to this faction is a proposal.
